subject.title: Cron session accumulation can silently exhaust agent context window — no guardrails or warnings

question: Should #38730 remain the umbrella for cron/session guardrails, or should maintainers make #89666/#90194 the retention canonical item and #89739 the cadence canonical item, then close this issue after those decisions land?
rationale: The source bug is real, but the requested scope combines cleanup semantics, session-state compatibility, cadence policy, and context-warning UX, so automation should not choose the final product split while active maintainer-reviewed PRs exist.

options.title: Keep Umbrella Open
options.body: Keep #38730 open until #90194/#89666 and #89739 land or are explicitly rejected, then re-triage any leftover warning UX.

options.title: Narrow To Retention
options.body: Treat #89666/#90194 as the only canonical fix and close this broader issue once retention semantics are settled.

options.title: Split New Warning Work
options.body: Create a separate product issue for context-window warning UX and let this issue close after the retention/cadence items are linked.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella Open
recommendation.body: Keep #38730 open until #90194/#89666 and #89739 land or are explicitly rejected, then re-triage any leftover warning UX.

likelyOwner.reason: openperf owns the active candidate retention PR that most directly decides whether the core data-retention slice is solved.
